stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s price slipped 1.0% today, leaving it 1.2% below its 52‑week high and still 38% above its 52‑week low. The modest 0.2% monthly gain follows a strong 25.6% YTD rise, suggesting the stock is consolidating near the top of its range. Investors should watch upcoming product cycle news and any guidance on services revenue for the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft fell 0.3% on the day and sits 2.1% shy of its 52‑week peak while remaining 51% above its 52‑week trough. A 6.0% gain over the past month and a 13.2% YTD increase indicate steady momentum despite short‑term softness. Key focus will be the next earnings release and cloud‑services growth outlook.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA dropped 0.3% and is now 9.5% below its 52‑week high, though still 31.4% above its low. After a 4.8% decline over the month, the stock’s YTD gain of 14.9% shows resilience amid a broader pullback. Investors should monitor GPU demand trends and any guidance on AI‑related revenue.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet slipped 1.1% today, trading 15.4% under its 52‑week high while 36.2% above its low. The 4.1% monthly decline follows an 8.2% YTD rise, indicating a modest correction. The next earnings report and ad‑spend trends will be the primary watch points.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon edged up 0.1% and remains 7.5% below its 52‑week high, still 32.1% above its low. A modest 1.6% gain across both the week and month adds to a 16.0% YTD increase, suggesting a stable near‑mid‑range position. Look for retail‑season sales data and cloud‑business performance as near‑term drivers.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta fell 1.6% and is 10.7% under its 52‑week high, though 32.3% above its low. The 6.3% monthly decline follows a modest 7.0% YTD rise, highlighting a cautious market stance. Investor attention should focus on user growth metrics and the rollout of AI features in its platforms.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla rose 1.5% on the day but stays 23.7% below its 52‑week high, while still 25.3% above its low. The stock is down 14.7% YTD, with only a slight 0.4% dip over the past month, reflecting a bearish longer‑term trend. Watch for production updates and any policy changes affecting EV incentives as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom slipped 0.1% and is 30.3% beneath its 52‑week high, yet only 14.3% above its low, marking a broad pullback. The 3.3% YTD decline and 7.8% monthly drop suggest weakening momentum. Key focus will be the upcoming earnings and guidance on its semiconductor and infrastructure segments.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD fell 0.6% but remains 17.7% below its 52‑week high while soaring 180% above its low, reflecting a massive rally. A 13.1% monthly decline follows an extraordinary 139.3% YTD gain, indicating a potential topping. Investors should watch the next earnings beat and any signs of demand slowdown in the GPU/CPU markets.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has rebounded 1.2% today but remains 53.1% below its 52‑week high, trading near the lower end of its range. The stock’s 11.4% drop over the past month and 32.1% YTD decline highlight lingering pressure on cloud margins. Watch the upcoming earnings guidance for signs of stabilization in its cloud services revenue.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is flat today, still 8.3% shy of its 52‑week peak but up 61.8% from its 52‑week low, reflecting a long‑term recovery. Recent weekly and monthly gains suggest momentum returning after a weak start to the year. Investors should focus on the next product‑release cycle and any updates to its AI‑driven CRM suite.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan rose 0.5% and sits 7.7% below its 52‑week high, comfortably above its low point. The modest weekly gain and 5% YTD rise indicate steady earnings momentum amid a resilient banking environment. Key watch: upcoming Fed policy signals and the bank’s loan‑loss reserve trends.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America gained 0.5% but remains 21.5% under its 52‑week high, with a 12.6% monthly decline and an 8% YTD loss. The stock’s volatility reflects concerns over interest‑rate pressures on net interest margins. Investors should monitor the bank’s deposit growth and credit‑quality metrics in the next earnings report.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is up 0.9% and is trading at its 52‑week high, having risen 38.1% from its low. Strong monthly and YTD performance underscores robust transaction volumes and pricing power. The next catalyst is the company’s quarterly volume guidance and any shifts in consumer‑spending trends.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard rose 0.7% and is also at its 52‑week high, up 32% from its low. Consistent weekly and monthly gains point to continued strength in digital payments adoption. Watch for the upcoming earnings beat expectations and any updates on cross‑border fee trends.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix slipped 1.7% and remains 44.7% below its 52‑week high, though it is slightly above its low point. The 6.4% monthly decline and 24.5% YTD drop highlight subscriber growth concerns. Investors should focus on the next content slate rollout and any guidance on churn rates.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly jumped 3.5% and is trading at its 52‑week high, up 61.6% from its low, with strong weekly and monthly gains. The stock’s momentum reflects robust pipeline progress and pricing power in its diabetes franchise. Key watch: upcoming FDA decisions and quarterly sales guidance for its new obesity drug.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth rose 3.0% and sits 3.3% below its 52‑week high, up 63.8% from its low, with solid weekly and monthly advances. The health‑insurer’s performance is buoyed by strong enrollment trends and cost‑control initiatives. Investors should keep an eye on Medicare Advantage enrollment data and any guidance on medical‑cost inflation.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has rallied 2.2% today and 4.3% over the past week, but remains 6.8% below its 52‑week high and still 42.6% above its 52‑week low, indicating room for upside. The stock’s YTD gain of 27.1% reflects strong earnings momentum. Investors should watch upcoming drug pipeline updates and any guidance on cost pressures.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart slipped 0.7% on the day after a solid 5.0% weekly gain, trading 12.0% under its 52‑week high while still 18.1% above its low. The 9.7% monthly rise and modest 5.2% YTD performance suggest steady consumer demand. Key focus will be same‑store sales trends and the impact of its low‑price strategy on margins.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco edged down 0.1% but is up 4.2% week‑over‑week, sitting 9.0% below its 52‑week peak and 17.5% above its trough, with a strong 10.7% monthly gain. The 16.9% YTD increase underscores robust membership renewal. Watch membership renewal rates and any shifts in discretionary spending that could affect basket size.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot rose 1.7% today, gaining 7.2% over the week, yet remains 17.7% shy of its 52‑week high while 12.1% above its low. A 6.0% monthly rise contrasts with a -6.9% YTD decline, reflecting a recent earnings bounce. Investors should monitor housing market data and the company’s inventory positioning ahead of the spring build‑out season.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil slipped 0.2% intraday but is up 2.2% weekly, trading just 0.6% below its 52‑week high and 62.4% above its low, buoyed by a 12.4% monthly gain. The 47.9% YTD surge highlights strong oil price tailwinds. The next catalyst is the upcoming earnings report and any guidance on capital allocation amid volatile crude markets.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola ticked up 0.1% and is 0.4% below its 52‑week high, still 41.2% above its low, with a 7.3% monthly rise and a 37.9% YTD gain. The modest weekly gain of 3.8% suggests steady demand. Watch for volume‑based pricing updates and the impact of emerging‑market growth on earnings.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney gained 1.9% today, 2.8% over the week, and sits 2.9% under its 52‑week high while 21.8% above its low, with a 7.1% monthly increase but only a 0.6% YTD rise. The stock is near the top of its range after recent content and streaming improvements. Investors should focus on the upcoming earnings release and the performance of its parks and streaming segments.
